outcome: No proof, disproof, or new computational progress on the square-freeness of Euclid numbers (E_n = primorial(p_n) + 1) has appeared since 26 January 2024; the question remains exactly as open as before, with computational verification still resting on Wagstaff's 1993 check of the first 43 terms.
summary: The question 'Are all Euclid numbers square-free?' — i.e., is E_n = 1 + product of the first n primes never divisible by any prime squared — remains open with no relevant activity found since the frozen revision date. The current Wikipedia article on Euclid numbers (checked live, not just the frozen 2024 revision) still lists this as an explicit open question, unchanged in substance from January 2024. The OEIS entry A006862 for Euclid numbers has one substantive comment added in the window, on 17 November 2024 by Antti Karttunen, but it establishes only that Euclid numbers are a subsequence of A048103 (numbers not divisible by p^p for any prime p) — a strictly weaker property than squarefreeness (squarefree numbers are themselves a proper subsequence of A048103, per the OEIS wiki page for A048103). This is consistent with, but does not advance, the squarefree question; it does not narrow which Euclid number could first fail to be squarefree. It is best read as incidental commentary rather than progress on the stated problem, so it does not change the status. Nyblom's 2008/2009 result (published as 'Euclid numbers are free from powers' in 2014, and referenced identically before and after the frozen date) predates the window and only rules out Euclid numbers being *perfect powers* — again a different and weaker-adjacent statement than squarefreeness, and it was already known before January 2024, so it is not new either way. Searches for arXiv preprints, Wagstaff-style computational extensions, and factordb records turned up nothing addressing squarefreeness specifically; a February 2026 arXiv paper ('A generalisation of the Euclid–Mullin sequences', arXiv:2601.21901) that surfaced in search results concerns the unrelated Euclid–Mullin sequence (where each term is a prime factor of one plus the product of previous terms) and cyclotomic residue-class questions, not squarefreeness of primorial+1 numbers — a related-but-distinct problem under §3.1's variant rule, so it is excluded from scope. No AI system involvement was found anywhere in the (nonexistent) progress. Confidence is high that nothing has happened: this is a narrow, well-defined, decades-old question in a well-indexed subfield (OEIS, Wikipedia, arXiv, MathWorld) with essentially no research traffic, and no source of any kind — preprint, blog, survey, database comment — post-dating 26 January 2024 touches it.
competing_reading: One could argue the November 2024 OEIS comment establishing Euclid numbers as a subsequence of A048103 constitutes minor 'progress' in a loose sense, since A048103 membership is a necessary (though far weaker) condition than squarefreeness, and it is new information about the sequence posted inside the window. But it does not narrow the actual squarefree question (a number can be in A048103, e.g. 5^4=625, without being squarefree), so under the case-vs-variant/no-narrowing test in §3.1 it does not count as touching this bullet's status. If a future record disagreed, it would most likely relabel this `progress` rather than `partial` or higher.
what_would_settle_it: Either an explicit proof that no Euclid number is divisible by any prime square, a single exhibited counterexample (an E_n divisible by some q^2), or even an extension of Wagstaff's computational verification (currently to n=43) to further terms would count as movement; none of these has been found.
